information_categories.credentials: Password, access token, private key, authenticated session material; credential role must have source evidence.
information_categories.personal_identifiers: Name, contact address, account identity or persistent linkable identifier; linkage and context matter.
information_categories.financial: Payment, account, transaction or other confidential financial information.
information_categories.health: Medical, health or other person-linked special-category information.
information_categories.private_content: User payload, communication, document or request content with explicit confidentiality or personal context.
information_categories.infrastructure_secrets: Secret service configuration or internal access material with evidence of its role.
information_categories.context_dependent: IP address, path, URL, diagnostic metadata and ordinary IDs require contextual evidence; not automatically sensitive.

supported: Historical source evidence establishes sensitive meaning and the output unit or proven path; runtime existence and exposure remain unverified.
suspected: A specific reviewable source/field/category clue exists but sensitivity, connection or residual-output semantics needs evidence.
not_found: Necessary checks completed in the stated boundary and scope with evidence-backed absence of sensitive residual information.
unknown: Evidence or support does not permit a sensitivity finding; absence of keyword matches is insufficient.
name_only: Names and reference labels are clues, never target truth or verified transformation semantics.
masking: Require the actual historical implementation, selected fields, retained characters and context. Partial masking may retain identifying or secret information.
hashing: A function name is not proof. Inspect actual transform, input entropy, salts/keys and linkability when available. Unsupported properties remain unknown; never invert or reconstruct values.
test_values: Record test/example/generated/development scope independently. Fictional examples may test semantics but do not establish production exposure or a real credential.
placeholders: Only source-supported fixed placeholders can support non-sensitive output; a constant is not automatically a placeholder or safe.
current_automatic_fixed_value_allowlist: Python booleans and null, exact MASKED placeholder and fixed words ok/done/started/finished can support bounded checks. General strings remain unknown even without a regex match. All transformations and selected fields must still have necessary evidence.
current_literal_credential_rule: Direct literal credential assignment syntax keyed by password/passwd/secret/api_key/access_token/authorization, excluding supported placeholders, provides static category evidence only. A matching literal nested inside a transform or boolean expression remains suspected until that path is checked. Test scope and runtime confirmation remain independent.
fixed_output: Verify the fixed bytes semantically and that the target dynamic information does not reach this boundary; a sensitive constant can have a zero-hop risk path.
formal_parameters: A formal parameter is a trace stopping boundary, not a verified ultimate business source.
relation_types: Value propagation, derived propagation, possible relations, type/schema descriptions and unresolved boundaries remain distinct.
severity: No calibrated severity or probability is assumed. Preserve null with its missing-context reason unless a future version defines and validates a rubric.
runtime_boundary: Static risk at call_argument, log_record or formatted_output never establishes runtime triggering, disk persistence, exfiltration or confirmed leakage.
review_truth: Rule, AI and human ledgers are separate. Unexecuted review remains pending. Only independently supplied eligible human evidence can support evaluation truth.
